translations.idiomatic: We, of little merit, now inherit that thread; we mourn without end, torn between grief for the dead and care for the living.

sentences.zh: 夫昭穆之義，固宜本之天屬。

translations.literal: The meaning of zhao and mu, solidly, ought to root in Heaven’s kin.
translations.idiomatic: The temple order of zhao and mu must rest on true blood descent.

sentences.zh: 繼體承基，古今常道。

translations.literal: Continuing the body and receiving the foundation is the constant way of ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: To continue the royal person and receive the foundation is the unchanging rule of all ages.

sentences.zh: 宜上嗣顯宗，以修本統。」

translations.literal: One ought to ascend in succession to Xianzong, thereby to repair the root line.”
translations.idiomatic: We should therefore return the succession to Emperor Cheng’s line and restore the legitimate descent.”

sentences.zh: 十二月，加涼州刺史張玄靚爲大都督隴右諸軍事、護羌校尉、西平公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Governor of Liang Zhang Xuanjing was added grand commander-in-chief of military affairs in Longyou, colonel protecting the Qiang, and duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhang Xuanjing, governor of Liang, was promoted to overall command in Longyou, Qiang colonel, and duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 隆和元年春正月壬子，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longhe, spring, the first month, on renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed; the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Longhe year, on renzi in the first spring month, a general amnesty was declared and the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，減田稅，畝收二升。

translations.literal: On jiayin, field tax was reduced; per mu two sheng were collected.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin land tax was cut so that only two sheng per mu was levied.

sentences.zh: 是月，慕容暐將呂護、傅末波攻陷小壘，以逼洛陽。

translations.literal: In that month, the generals of Murong Wei, Lu Hu and Fu Mobo, attacked and took the lesser fort, thereby pressing Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Lu Hu and Fu Mobo, generals of Murong Wei, seized an outwork and tightened the noose on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 二月辛未，以輔國將軍、吳國內史庾希爲北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史，鎮下邳；

translations.literal: On xinwei of the second month, with General Who Supports the State and administrator of the interior of Wu, Yu Xi, as north central commandant and governor of the two provinces Xu and Yan, garrisoning Xiapi;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the second month Yu Xi, general supporting the state and interior administrator of Wu, became north central commandant and dual governor of Xu and Yan, based at Xiapi;

sentences.zh: 前鋒監軍、龍驤將軍袁眞爲西中郎將、監護豫司幷冀四州諸軍事、豫州刺史，鎮汝南，並假節。

translations.literal: vanguard supervisor of the army, General of Dragon Martial Yuan Zhen as general of the west central command, supervisor and protector of military affairs in the four provinces of Yu, Si, Bing, and Ji, and governor of Yu, garrisoning Runan, both with credential staffs.
translations.idiomatic: while Yuan Zhen, vanguard army supervisor and dragon martial general, became general of the central west command with oversight of Yu, Si, Bing, and Ji and governorship of Yu from Runan—both posts carried the ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: 丙子，尊所生周氏爲皇太妃。

translations.literal: On bingzi, they honored his birth mother, Lady Zhou, as grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor’s natural mother, Lady Zhou, was elevated to grand consort.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On jiayin of the third month, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon on jiayin in the third month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，旱。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth summer month was stricken by drought.

sentences.zh: 詔出輕繫，振困乏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered release of light prisoners and relief for the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: An edict freed minor convicts and aided the starving.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，梁州地震，浩亹山崩。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Liang Province earthquake; Haomen Mountain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Liang Province quaked and Haomen Mountain gave way.

sentences.zh: 呂護復寇洛陽。

translations.literal: Lu Hu again raided Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hu struck Luoyang again.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，輔國將軍、河南太守戴施奔于宛。

translations.literal: On yiyou, General Who Supports the State and Prefect of Henan Dai Shi fled to Wan.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Dai Shi, general supporting the state and prefect of Henan, fled to Wan.

sentences.zh: 五月丁巳，遣北中郎將庾希、竟陵太守鄧遐以舟師救洛陽。

translations.literal: On dingsi of the fifth month, they sent North Central Commandant Yu Xi and prefect of Jingling Deng Xia with a river force to relieve Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the fifth month Yu Xi and Deng Xia, prefect of Jingling, were sent upriver with a fleet to relieve Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，呂護等退守小平津。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Lu Hu and others withdrew to guard Little Ping Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month Lu Hu’s force drew back to hold Little Ping Ford.

sentences.zh: 進琅邪王奕爲侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Yi was advanced palace attendant, great general of agile cavalry, with authority to open an office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Langye was promoted to palace attendant and great general of agile cavalry with an independent office.

sentences.zh: 鄧遐進屯新城，庾希部將何謙及慕容暐將劉則戰于檀丘，破之。

translations.literal: Deng Xia advanced to encamp at Xincheng; the subordinate general of Yu Xi, He Qian, and the general of Murong Wei, Liu Ze, battled at Tanqiu; they broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Xia moved to Xincheng; He Qian under Yu Xi met Murong Wei’s Liu Ze at Tanqiu and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 八月，西中郎將袁眞進次汝南，運米五萬斛以饋洛陽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, General of the West Central Command Yuan Zhen advanced and halted at Runan, transported fifty thousand hu of grain to feed Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yuan Zhen, general of the central west command, advanced to Runan and shipped fifty thousand hu of grain to supply Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，賜貧乏者米，人五斛。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, they gave grain to the poor and destitute, five hu per person.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month the poor were issued five hu of grain each.

sentences.zh: 章武王珍薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhen of Zhangwu died.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhen, prince of Zhangwu, died.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On wuwu of the twelfth month, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon on wuwu in the twelfth month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「戎旅路次，未得輕簡賦役。

translations.literal: An edict said: “The army on the road; we have not been able lightly to reduce levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ran: “While troops are on the march we cannot lightly cut taxes or labor service.

sentences.zh: 玄象失度，亢旱爲患，豈政事未洽，將有板築、渭濱之士邪！

translations.literal: The celestial images have lost their measure; severe drought is the calamity—is it that government affairs are not harmonized, or that there are men of Banzhu or by the Wei’s bank!
translations.idiomatic: The heavens are out of joint and killing drought stalks the land—are our policies still awry, or are we missing the wise men Ban once raised or the sage by the Wei!

sentences.zh: 其搜揚隱滯，蠲除苛碎，詳議法令，咸從損耍。

translations.literal: Let them search out and raise the hidden and stagnant, remit harsh and petty measures, deliberate on laws and ordinances in detail, and all follow curtailment and essential points.”
translations.idiomatic: Search out hidden talent, repeal harsh petty rules, review the code in detail, and let every measure be pared to what truly matters.”

sentences.zh: 」庾希自下邳退鎮山陽，袁眞自汝南退鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: ” Yu Xi from Xiapi withdrew to garrison Shanyang; Yuan Zhen from Runan withdrew to garrison Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yu Xi fell back from Xiapi to Shanyang, and Yuan Zhen from Runan to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 興寧元年春二月己亥，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingning, spring, the second month, on jihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed; the reign title was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Xingning year, on jihai in the second spring month, a general amnesty was issued and the era name changed.

sentences.zh: 三月壬寅，皇太妃薨于琅邪第。

translations.literal: On renyin of the third month, the grand consort died at the Langye residence.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the third month the grand consort died at the Langye mansion.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝奔喪，詔司徒、會稽王昱總內外衆務。

translations.literal: On guimao, the emperor went to mourning; an edict ordered the minister of education, Prince Hui of Kuaiji, to oversee all inner and outer affairs of the host.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor went into mourning while Prince Hui of Kuaiji, minister of education, was ordered to oversee all court and camp business.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，慕容暐寇滎陽，太守劉遠奔魯陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Murong Wei raided Xingyang; Prefect Liu Yuan fled to Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month Murong Wei struck Xingyang and Prefect Liu Yuan bolted for Luyang.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，揚州地震，湖瀆溢。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Yang Province earthquake; lakes overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Yang Province quaked and lakes burst their banks.

sentences.zh: 五月，加征西大將軍桓溫侍中、大司馬、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書事、假黃鉞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they added to Great General Who Campaigns West Huan Wen the posts of palace attendant, grand marshal, commander-in-chief of military affairs inner and outer, supervisor of Secretariat business, and ceremonial yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Huan Wen was given palace attendant rank, the grand marshalcy, command over all military affairs civil and military, supervision of the Secretariat, and the ceremonial yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 復以西中郎將袁眞都督司、冀、幷三州諸軍事，北中郎將廋希都督青州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Again with General of the West Central Command Yuan Zhen as commander-in-chief of military affairs in the three provinces of Si, Ji, and Bing, and North Central Commandant Yu Xi (written 廋 in the text) as commander-in-chief of military affairs in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, general of the central west command, was again placed over Si, Ji, and Bing, while Yu Xi, north central commandant, received sole command of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，慕容暐陷密城，滎陽太守劉遠奔于江陵。

translations.literal: On guimao, Murong Wei took Mi city; Prefect of Xingyang Liu Yuan fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Murong Wei seized Mi, and Liu Yuan, prefect of Xingyang, fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，張天錫弑涼州刺史、西平公張玄靚，自稱大將軍、護羌校尉、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Tianxi murdered Governor of Liang and Duke of Xiping Zhang Xuanjing, and himself styled great general, colonel protecting the Qiang, shepherd of Liang, and duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month Zhang Tianxi assassinated Zhang Xuanjing, governor of Liang and duke of Xiping, and declared himself great general, Qiang colonel, governor of Liang, and duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，葬章皇太妃。

translations.literal: On dingyou, they buried the Honored Grand Consort Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the late Honored Grand Consort Zhang was buried.

sentences.zh: 八月，有星孛于角亢，入天市。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, there was a broom star in Jue and Kang; it entered the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a comet appeared in the lodges Horn and Neck and entered the Celestial Market.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，大司馬桓溫帥衆北伐。

translations.literal: On renxu of the ninth month, Grand Marshal Huan Wen led the host on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the ninth month Grand Marshal Huan Wen marched north at the head of a large army.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以皇子生，大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai, because an imperial son was born, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the birth of a prince occasioned a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲申，立陳留王世子恢爲王。

translations.literal: On jiashen of winter, the tenth month, they established the heir apparent of the Prince of Chenliu, Hui, as prince.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the tenth winter month Hui, heir of the Prince of Chenliu, was invested as prince in his own right.

sentences.zh: 十一月，姚襄故將張駿殺江州督護趙毗，焚武昌，略府藏以叛，江州刺史桓沖討斬之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the former general of Yao Xiang, Zhang Jun, killed Jiang Province protector Zhao Pi, burned Wuchang, plundered the treasury stores in revolt; Governor of Jiang Huan Chong campaigned, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhang Jun, once Yao Xiang’s officer, murdered protector Zhao Pi, torched Wuchang, looted the granaries, and mutinied; Huan Chong, governor of Jiang, crushed the rising and executed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，慕容暐將慕容塵攻陳留太守袁披于長平。

translations.literal: In this year, the general of Murong Wei, Murong Chen, attacked Prefect of Chenliu Yuan Pi at Changping.
translations.idiomatic: That year Murong Chen, a general of Murong Wei, besieged Yuan Pi, prefect of Chenliu, at Changping.

sentences.zh: 汝南太守朱斌承虛襲許昌，克之。

translations.literal: Prefect of Runan Zhu Bin took advantage of emptiness to raid Xuchang and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bin, prefect of Runan, struck Xuchang while it was weak and captured it.

sentences.zh: 二年春二月庚寅，江陵地震。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, the second month, on gengyin, Jiangling earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the second spring month of the second year Jiangling was shaken by an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐將慕容評襲許昌，潁川太守李福死之。

translations.literal: The general of Murong Wei, Murong Ping, raided Xuchang; Prefect of Yingchuan Li Fu died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping, Murong Wei’s commander, hit Xuchang; Li Fu, prefect of Yingchuan, fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 評遂侵汝南，太守朱斌遁于壽陽。

translations.literal: Ping thereupon invaded Runan; Prefect Zhu Bin fled to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping then pushed into Runan, and Zhu Bin fled to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 又進圍陳郡，太守朱輔嬰城固守。

translations.literal: He further advanced to besiege Chen commandery; Prefect Zhu Fu drew up the defenses and firmly held the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Chen commandery, where Zhu Fu sealed the walls and stood a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 桓溫遣江夏相劉岵擊退之。

translations.literal: Huan Wen sent Chancellor of Jiangxia Liu Hu to strike and repulse him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen dispatched Liu Hu, chancellor of Jiangxia, who drove him back.

sentences.zh: 改左軍將軍爲遊擊將軍，罷右軍、前軍、後軍將軍五校三將官。

translations.literal: They changed the general of the left army to general of roaming attack, and abolished the five camps and three general posts of the right army, front army, and rear army.
translations.idiomatic: The left army general’s title was changed to roaming strike general, and the right, front, and rear army commands with their five-camp establishments were abolished.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝親耕藉田。

translations.literal: On guimao, the emperor personally plowed the ritual field.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor performed the sacred plowing at the ceremonial field.

sentences.zh: 三月庚戌朔，大閱戶人，嚴法禁，稱爲庚戌制。

translations.literal: On gengxu of the third month, the first day of the month, they greatly reviewed registered households and tightened laws and prohibitions; it was called the gengxu system.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon on gengxu in the third month the court conducted a sweeping household census and stiffened the code—the measure went down in history as the gengxu regulations.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝不悆。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the emperor was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the emperor fell seriously ill.

sentences.zh: 帝雅好黃老，斷穀，餌長生藥，服食過多，遂中毒，不識萬機，崇德太后復臨朝攝政。

translations.literal: The emperor had long favored Huang-Lao, abstained from grain, and took longevity drugs; because ingestion was excessive, he was poisoned, did not recognize the myriad threads of state; Empress Dowager Chongde again assumed regency from behind the screen.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign had dabbled in Huang-Lao asceticism, avoided grain, and swallowed elixirs in dangerous quantity until he was poisoned and could no longer govern; Empress Dowager Chongde resumed the regency.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲申，慕容暐遣其將李洪侵許昌，王師敗績于懸瓠，朱斌奔于淮南，朱輔退保彭城。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiashen, Murong Wei sent his general Li Hong to invade Xuchang; the royal army was routed at Xuanhu; Zhu Bin fled to Huainan; Zhu Fu withdrew to guard Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the fourth summer month Murong Wei’s Li Hong struck Xuchang; the imperial army was shattered at Xuanhu; Zhu Bin bolted for the Huai region and Zhu Fu retreated to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓溫遣西中郎將袁眞、江夏相劉岵等鑿楊儀道以通運，溫帥舟師次于合肥，慕容塵復屯許昌。

translations.literal: Huan Wen sent General of the West Central Command Yuan Zhen, Chancellor of Jiangxia Liu Hu, and others to cut the Yang-Yi waterway to open transport; Wen led a river fleet and halted at Hefei; Murong Chen again encamped at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen ordered Yuan Zhen, Liu Hu, and others to open the Yang-Yi canal for supply; he himself brought a fleet to Hefei while Murong Chen reoccupied Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 五月，遷陳人于陸以避之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they relocated the people of Chen to Lu to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the population of Chen was moved inland to Lu to escape the Yan advance.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以揚州刺史王述爲尚書令、衛將軍。

translations.literal: On wuchen, with Governor of Yang Wang Shu as director of the Secretariat and general who guards the court.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Shu, governor of Yang, became director of the Secretariat and general guarding the court.

sentences.zh: 以桓溫爲揚州牧、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: With Huan Wen as shepherd of Yang and supervisor of Secretariat business.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was named governor of Yang and overseer of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壬申，遣使喻溫入相，溫不從。

translations.literal: On renshen, they sent envoys to instruct Wen to enter as chancellor; Wen did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen envoys urged Huan Wen to come to the capital as chief minister; he refused.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁卯，復徵溫入朝。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingmao, they again summoned Wen to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the seventh autumn month he was summoned to court again.

sentences.zh: 八月，溫至赭圻，遂城而居之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wen arrived at Zheqi, thereupon walled it and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Huan Wen reached Zheqi, threw up fortifications, and settled in.

sentences.zh: 苻堅別帥侵河南，慕容暐寇洛陽。

translations.literal: A separate commander of Fu Jian invaded Henan; Murong Wei raided Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: A detached column of Fu Jian’s crossed the river into Henan while Murong Wei struck Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，冠軍將軍陳祐留長史沈勁守洛陽，帥衆奔新城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, General Who Vanquishes Champions Chen You left Chief Clerk Shen Jing to defend Luoyang, and led the host to flee to Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chen You, general who vanquishes champions, left Shen Jing to hold Luoyang while he withdrew the main force to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月庚申，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, the first month, on gengshen, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the third year’s first spring month Empress Wang passed away.

sentences.zh: 二月乙未，以右將軍桓豁監荊州揚州之義城雍州之京兆諸軍事、領南蠻校尉、荊州刺史；

translations.literal: On yiwei of the second month, with General of the Right Huan Huo as supervisor of military affairs in Yicheng of Jing and Yang, Jingzhao of Yong, concurrently colonel of the southern Man, and governor of Jing;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Huan Huo, general of the right, was put in charge of Yicheng in Jing and Yang, Jingzhao in Yong, named southern Man colonel, and made governor of Jing;

sentences.zh: 桓沖監江州荊州之江夏隨郡豫州之汝南西陽新蔡潁川六郡諸軍事、南中郎將、江州刺史，領南蠻校尉，並假節。

translations.literal: Huan Chong as supervisor of military affairs in the six commanderies Jiangxia and Suijun of Jiang and Jing, Runan, Xiyang, Xincai, and Yingchuan of Yu, south central commandant, governor of Jiang, concurrently colonel of the southern Man, both with credential staffs.
translations.idiomatic: while Huan Chong supervised Jiang’s Jiangxia and Suijun plus Yu’s Runan, Xiyang, Xincai, and Yingchuan as south central commandant and governor of Jiang with the southern Man colonelcy—both brothers held the ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: 丙申，帝崩于西堂，時年二十五。

translations.literal: On bingshen, the emperor died in the West Hall; at the time he was twenty-five sui.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor died in the West Hall at the age of twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 葬安平陵。

translations.literal: He was buried at Anping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was interred at Anping Ling.

sentences.zh: 海西公

translations.literal: The Duke of Haixi.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 廢帝諱奕，字延齡，哀帝之母弟也。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor had the taboo name Yi, courtesy name Yanling, and was the younger brother by the same mother of Emperor Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed sovereign, personal name Yi and courtesy name Yanling, was Emperor Ai’s full younger brother.

sentences.zh: 咸康八年封爲東海王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Xiankang he was enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Xiankang year he was invested prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 永和八年拜散騎常侍，尋加鎮軍將軍；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yonghe he was appointed cavalier attendant for regular service; shortly he was added general who stabilizes the army;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Yonghe year he became cavalier attendant for regular service and soon after general stabilizing the army;

sentences.zh: 升平四年拜車騎將軍。

translations.literal: in the fourth year of Shengping he was appointed general of chariots and cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: and in the fourth Shengping year general of chariots and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 五年，改封琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, his fief was changed to Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his title was transferred from Donghai to prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 隆和初，轉侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longhe, he was transferred palace attendant, great general of agile cavalry, with authority to open an office and parity of ceremony with the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longhe era he moved to palace attendant, great general of agile cavalry, with an independent office and Three-Dukes honors.

sentences.zh: 興寧三年二月丙申，哀帝崩，無嗣。

translations.literal: On bingshen of the second month of the third year of Xingning, Emperor Ai died, without heir.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the second month of the third Xingning year Emperor Ai died childless.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，皇太后詔曰：「帝遂不救厥疾，艱禍仍臻，遺緒泯然，哀慟切心。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the empress dowager issued an edict saying: “The emperor has finally not been saved from his illness; hardships and calamities have come in succession; the thread of succession is extinguished; grief and pain cut the heart.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the empress dowager proclaimed: “The sovereign could not be saved; disaster has struck again and again, the line is broken, and our hearts are torn with grief.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王奕，明德茂親，屬當儲嗣，宜奉祖宗，纂承大統。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye Yi, of brilliant virtue and luxuriant kinship, belongs to the heir’s position; he ought to serve the ancestors and continue the great line.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Langye, a man of shining virtue and the nearest royal blood, is the rightful heir and should mount the throne to honor the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 便速正大禮，以寧人神。

translations.literal: Let him speedily set right the great rites, thereby to bring peace to men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Let the great accession rites proceed at once, for the peace of the realm and the shades.

sentences.zh: 」于是百官奉迎于琅邪第。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the hundred officials received and welcomed him at the Langye princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: ” The full bureaucracy escorted him from the Langye mansion.

sentences.zh: 是日，卽皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: That day, he assumed the imperial throne; a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The same day he ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月壬申，葬哀皇帝于安平陵。

translations.literal: On renshen of the third month, they buried Emperor Ai at Anping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the third month Emperor Ai was buried at Anping Ling.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，散騎常侍、河間王欽薨。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Cavalier Attendant for Regular Service, Prince Qin of Hejian, Qin, died.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Sima Qin, prince of Hejian and cavalier attendant for regular service, died.

sentences.zh: 丙子，慕容暐將慕容恪陷洛陽，寧朔將軍竺瑤奔于襄陽，冠軍長史、揚武將軍沈勁死之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the general of Murong Wei, Murong Ke, took Luoyang; General Who Calms the Caitiffs Zhu Yao fled to Xiangyang; champion chief clerk and General Who Rouses Martial Prowess Shen Jing died in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Murong Ke, Murong Wei’s commander, captured Luoyang; Zhu Yao, general calming the caitiffs, fled to Xiangyang; Shen Jing, champion chief clerk and general rousing martial prowess, died defending the city.

sentences.zh: 夏六月戊子，使持節、都督益寧二州諸軍事、鎮西將軍、益州刺史、建城公周撫卒。

translations.literal: On wuzi of summer, the sixth month, Zhou Chu, bearer of credentials, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the two provinces of Yi and Ning, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Yi, and Duke of Jiancheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in the sixth summer month Zhou Chu died—he had held the staff, commanded Yi and Ning, led the western expedition, governed Yi, and borne the Jiancheng dukedom.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，匈奴左賢王衛辰、右賢王曹穀帥衆二萬侵苻堅杏城。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Xiongnu left worthy prince Wei Chen and right worthy prince Cao Gu led a host of twenty thousand to invade Fu Jian’s Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month the Xiongnu left and right worthy princes Wei Chen and Cao Gu brought twenty thousand horsemen against Fu Jian’s Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 己酉，改封會稽王昱爲琅邪王。

translations.literal: On jiyou, they changed the fief of Prince Hui of Kuaiji to Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Prince Hui of Kuaiji was transferred to the title of prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 壬子，立皇后庾氏。

translations.literal: On renzi, they established Empress Yu.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Lady Yu was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 封琅邪王昱子昌明爲會稽王。

translations.literal: They enfeoffed the son of Prince of Langye Hui, Changming, as Prince of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Hui’s son Changming was invested prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，梁州刺史司馬勳反，自稱成都王。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Governor of Liang Sima Xun rebelled, styling himself Prince of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Sima Xun, governor of Liang, rose in revolt and declared himself prince of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帥衆入劍閣，攻涪，西夷校尉毌丘暐棄城而遁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he led the host into Jian’ge, attacked Fucheng, and Colonel of the Western Yi Guanqiu Wei abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he forced Jian’ge and struck Fucheng; Guanqiu Wei, colonel of the western Yi, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，圍益州刺史周楚于成都，桓溫遣江夏相朱序救之。

translations.literal: On yimao, he besieged Governor of Yi Zhou Chu at Chengdu; Huan Wen sent Chancellor of Jiangxia Zhu Xu to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he invested Chengdu and penned Zhou Chu, governor of Yi; Huan Wen sent Zhu Xu, chancellor of Jiangxia, to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊戌，以會稽內史王彪之爲尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On wuxu of the twelfth month, with Administrator of the Interior of Kuaiji Wang Bianzhi as vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu in the twelfth month Wang Bianzhi, interior administrator of Kuaiji, became vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太和元年春二月己丑，以涼州刺史張天錫爲大將軍、都督隴右關中諸軍事、西平郡公。

translations.literal: On jichou of the second month of the first year of Taihe, with Governor of Liang Zhang Tianxi as great general, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Longyou and Guanzhong, and duke of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the second month of the first Taihe year Zhang Tianxi, governor of Liang, was named great general, commander over Longyou and Guanzhong, and duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以宣城內史桓秘爲持節、監梁益二州征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingshen, with Administrator of the Interior of Xuancheng Huan Mi as bearer of credentials, supervisor of military affairs in punitive expeditions in the two provinces of Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Huan Mi, interior administrator of Xuancheng, received the staff to supervise Liang and Yi in the western campaigns.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，旱。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, drought.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth summer month brought drought.

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅，皇后庾氏崩。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the fifth month, Empress Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the fifth month Empress Yu died.

sentences.zh: 朱序攻司馬勳于成都，衆潰，執勳，斬之。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu attacked Sima Xun at Chengdu; the host dispersed; he seized Xun and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu stormed Chengdu, shattered Sima Xun’s army, took him captive, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，葬孝皇后于敬平陵。

translations.literal: On guiyou of autumn, the seventh month, they buried Empress Xiao at Jingping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the seventh autumn month Empress Xiao was interred at Jingping Ling.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，曲赦梁、益二州。

translations.literal: On jiawu of the ninth month, they issued a partial amnesty for the two provinces Liang and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the ninth month Liang and Yi received a special amnesty.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛丑，苻堅將王猛、楊安攻南鄉，荊州刺史桓豁救之，師次新野而猛、安退。

translations.literal: On xinchou of winter, the tenth month, Fu Jian’s generals Wang Meng and Yang An attacked Nanxiang; Governor of Jing Huan Huo relieved them; the army halted at Xinye while Meng and An withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the tenth winter month Wang Meng and Yang An of Former Qin struck Nanxiang; Huan Huo, governor of Jing, marched to the relief and stopped at Xinye, whereupon Wang Meng and Yang An pulled back.

sentences.zh: 以會稽王昱爲丞相。

translations.literal: With Prince Hui of Kuaiji as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Kuaiji was appointed chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十二月，南陽人趙弘、趙憶等據宛城反，太守桓澹走保新野。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the men of Nanyang Zhao Hong and Zhao Yi and others occupied Wan city in revolt; Prefect Huan Dan fled to guard Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Zhao Hong, Zhao Yi, and others of Nanyang seized Wan; Huan Dan, the prefect, fled to Xinye.

sentences.zh: 慕容暐將慕容厲陷魯郡、高平。

translations.literal: The general of Murong Wei, Murong Li, took Lu commandery and Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Li, Murong Wei’s general, overran Lu and Gaoping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，北中郎將庾稀有罪，走入于海。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, the first month, North Central Commandant Yu Xi (written 稀 in the text) had a crime and fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Yu Xi, north central commandant, was implicated in a crime and fled out to sea.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，慕容暐將慕容塵寇竟陵，太守羅崇擊破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the general of Murong Wei, Murong Chen, raided Jingling; Prefect Luo Chong attacked and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month Murong Chen struck Jingling but Luo Chong, the prefect, repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將王猛寇涼州，張天錫距之，猛師敗績。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s general Wang Meng raided Liang Province; Zhang Tianxi opposed him; Meng’s army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng of Qin invaded Liang; Zhang Tianxi met him in the field and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 五月，右將軍桓豁擊趙憶，走之，進獲慕容暐將趙槃，送于京師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, General of the Right Huan Huo struck Zhao Yi, drove him off, advanced and captured the general of Murong Wei, Zhao Pan, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Huan Huo, general of the right, chased off Zhao Yi, captured Murong Wei’s Zhao Pan, and sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，以會稽內史郗愔爲都督徐兗青幽四州諸軍事、平北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, with Administrator of the Interior of Kuaiji Xi Yin as commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Xu, Yan, Qing, and You, General Who Pacifies the North, and governor of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth autumn month Xi Yin, interior administrator of Kuaiji, was named commander over Xu, Yan, Qing, and You, general pacifying the north, and governor of Xu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙巳，彭城王玄薨。

translations.literal: On yisi of winter, the tenth month, Prince Xuan of Pengcheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the tenth winter month Prince Xuan of Pengcheng died.

sentences.zh: 三年春三月丁巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, the third month, on dingsi, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon on dingsi in the third spring month of the third year the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸巳，雨雹，大風折木。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guisi, there was hail; a great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the fourth summer month hail fell and a gale snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 秋八月壬寅，尚書令、衛將軍、藍田侯王述卒。

translations.literal: On renyin of autumn, the eighth month, Director of the Secretariat, General Who Guards the Court, Marquis of Lantian Wang Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin in the eighth autumn month Wang Shu died—director of the Secretariat, general guarding the court, and marquis of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 四年夏四月庚戌，大司馬桓溫帥衆伐慕容暐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, summer, the fourth month, on gengxu, Grand Marshal Huan Wen led the host to campaign against Murong Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu in the fourth summer month Grand Marshal Huan Wen marched against Murong Wei.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛卯，暐將慕容垂帥衆距溫，溫擊敗之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on xinmao, Wei’s general Murong Chui led the host to oppose Wen; Wen struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the seventh autumn month Murong Chui blocked Huan Wen, who defeated him in battle.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，桓溫裨將鄧遐、朱序遇暐將傅末波于林渚，又大破之。

translations.literal: On wuyin of the ninth month, Huan Wen’s lieutenant-generals Deng Xia and Zhu Xu met Wei’s general Fu Mobo at Linzhu, and again greatly broke him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the ninth month Deng Xia and Zhu Xu, subordinates of Huan Wen, met Fu Mobo at Linzhu and won another crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 戊子，溫至枋頭。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Wen arrived at Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Huan Wen reached Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以糧運不繼，焚舟而歸。

translations.literal: On bingshen, because grain transport did not keep up, he burned the boats and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, his supplies exhausted, Huan Wen burned his fleet and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，慕容垂追敗溫後軍于襄邑。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Murong Chui pursued and defeated Wen’s rear army at Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Murong Chui overtook Huan Wen’s rearguard at Xiangyi and routed it.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，大星西流，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, a great star flowed westward; there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month a huge meteor streaked west with a roar like thunder.

sentences.zh: 己巳，溫收散卒，屯于山陽。

translations.literal: On jisi, Wen gathered scattered troops and encamped at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Huan Wen rallied his broken units and camped at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史袁眞以壽陽叛。

translations.literal: Governor of Yu Yuan Zhen rebelled with Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen, governor of Yu, mutinied and held Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛丑，桓溫自山陽及會稽王昱會于塗中，將謀後舉。

translations.literal: On xinchou of the eleventh month, Huan Wen from Shanyang and Prince Hui of Kuaiji met at Tuzhong, planning to arrange a later move.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the eleventh month Huan Wen joined Prince Hui of Kuaiji at Tuzhong to plot their next step.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂城廣陵而居之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he thereupon walled Guangling and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he fortified Guangling and took up residence.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月己亥，袁眞子雙之、愛之害梁國內史朱憲、汝南內史朱斌。

translations.literal: On jihai of the fifth year, spring, the first month, the sons of Yuan Zhen, Shuangzhi and Aizhi, killed Administrator of Liang Zhu Xian and Administrator of Runan Zhu Bin.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the fifth year’s first spring month Yuan Shuangzhi and Yuan Aizhi murdered Zhu Xian and Zhu Bin, the interior administrators of Liang and Runan.

sentences.zh: 二月癸酉，袁眞死，陳郡太守朱輔立眞子瑾嗣事，求救于慕容暐。

translations.literal: On guiyou of the second month, Yuan Zhen died; Prefect of Chen Zhu Fu established Zhen’s son Jin to handle affairs, and requested aid from Murong Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the second month Yuan Zhen died; Zhu Fu, prefect of Chen, set Yuan Jin, Zhen’s son, at the head of the rebellion and begged Murong Wei for help.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛未，桓溫部將竺瑤破瑾于武丘。

translations.literal: On xinwei of summer, the fourth month, Huan Wen’s subordinate Zhu Yao broke Jin at Wuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the fourth summer month Zhu Yao, Huan Wen’s officer, defeated Yuan Jin at Wuqiu.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On guiyou of autumn, the seventh month, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: At new moon on guiyou in the seventh autumn month the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 八月癸丑，桓溫擊袁瑾于壽陽，敗之。

translations.literal: On guichou of the eighth month, Huan Wen struck Yuan Jin at Shouyang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the eighth month Huan Wen attacked Yuan Jin at Shouyang and broke him.

sentences.zh: 九月，苻堅將猛伐慕容暐，陷其上黨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Fu Jian’s general Wang Meng campaigned against Murong Wei and took his Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Meng, Fu Jian’s foremost commander, marched against Murong Wei and seized Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 廣漢妖賊李弘與益州妖賊李金根聚衆反，弘自稱聖王，衆萬餘人，梓潼太守周虓討平之。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel of Guanghan, Li Hong, and the sorcerer-rebel of Yi Province, Li Jingen, gathered crowds and rebelled; Hong styled himself holy king; the host was more than ten thousand; Prefect of Zitong Zhou Xiao campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong of Guanghan and Li Jingen of Yi, self-styled holy men, raised over ten thousand fanatics; Li Hong called himself holy king until Zhou Xiao, prefect of Zitong, put down the rising.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，王猛大破慕容暐將慕容評于潞川。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wang Meng greatly defeated Murong Wei’s general Murong Ping at Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Wang Meng shattered Murong Ping at the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 十一月，猛克鄴，獲慕容暐，盡有其地。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Meng took Ye, captured Murong Wei, and entirely possessed his lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wang Meng took Ye, took Murong Wei prisoner, and annexed Yan.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，苻堅遣將王鑒來援袁瑾，將軍桓伊逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, spring, the first month, Fu Jian sent General Wang Jian to come relieve Yuan Jin; General Huan Yi met and struck him, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first spring month of the sixth year Fu Jian dispatched Wang Jian to aid Yuan Jin; Huan Yi intercepted him and won a major victory.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，桓溫克壽陽，斬袁瑾。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Huan Wen took Shouyang and beheaded Yuan Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Huan Wen stormed Shouyang and executed Yuan Jin.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰，監益寧二州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、益州刺史、建城公周楚卒。

translations.literal: On renchen of the third month, Zhou Chu, supervisor of military affairs in the two provinces of Yi and Ning, General Who Vanquishes Champions, Governor of Yi, and Duke of Jiancheng, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the third month Zhou Chu died—he had supervised Yi and Ning, held the champion general’s rank, governed Yi, and borne the Jiancheng dukedom.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊午，大赦，賜窮獨米，人五斛。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed; grain was given to the destitute and solitary, five hu per person.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the fourth summer month a general amnesty was declared and the needy received five hu of grain each.

sentences.zh: 苻堅將苻雅伐仇池，仇池公楊纂降之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian’s general Fu Ya campaigned against Qiuchi; Duke of Qiuchi Yang Zuan surrendered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Ya, a general of Fu Jian, attacked Qiuchi, and Yang Zuan, duke of Qiuchi, submitted.

sentences.zh: 六月，京都及丹陽、晉陵、吳郡、吳興、臨海並大水。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the capital region together with Danyang, Jinling, Wu commandery, Wuxing, and Linhai all had great flooding.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month catastrophic floods struck the capital and Danyang, Jinling, Wu, Wuxing, and Linhai alike.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，以前寧州刺史周仕孫爲假節、監益梁二州諸軍事、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, with former Governor of Ning Zhou Shisun Zhou as credential staff, supervisor of military affairs in the two provinces of Yi and Liang, and governor of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth autumn month Zhou Shisun, formerly governor of Ning, received the ceremonial staff to supervise Yi and Liang and govern Yi.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬子，高密王俊薨。

translations.literal: On renzi of winter, the tenth month, Prince Jun of Gaomi died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the tenth winter month Prince Jun of Gaomi died.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸卯，桓溫自廣陵屯于白石。

translations.literal: On guimao of the eleventh month, Huan Wen from Guangling encamped at Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the eleventh month Huan Wen moved from Guangling to camp at Baishi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詣闕，因圖廢立，誣帝在籓夙有痿疾，嬖人相龍、計好、朱靈寶等參侍內寢，而二美人田氏、孟氏生三男，長欲封樹，時人惑之，溫因諷太后以伊霍之舉。

translations.literal: On dingwei, he went to the palace gates, thereupon plotting deposition and enthronement; he slandered the emperor, saying that while still a prince he had long suffered impotence, while favorites Xiang Long, Ji Hao, Zhu Lingbao, and others attended him in the inner bedchamber, and two beauties, Lady Tian and Lady Meng, bore three sons; he was about to enfeoff and establish heirs; people of the time were perplexed; Wen thereupon insinuated to the empress dowager a deed in the manner of Yi Yin and Huo Guang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Huan Wen appeared at court intent on replacing the sovereign: he claimed the emperor had been impotent since his princely days while catamites named Xiang Long, Ji Hao, and Zhu Lingbao attended his couch and two concubines had produced three sons about to be named heirs—a tale the capital found scarcely credible—with which Huan Wen pressed the empress dowager to sanction an Yi–Huo-style change of ruler.

sentences.zh: 己酉，集百官于朝堂，宣崇德太后令曰：「王室艱難，穆、哀短祚，國嗣不育儲宮靡立。

translations.literal: On jiyou, he assembled the hundred officials at the court hall and proclaimed Empress Dowager Chongde’s order: “The royal house faces hardship; Mu and Ai enjoyed short fortunes; the heir has not been bred and the heir apparent’s palace stands empty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he gathered the bureaucracy in the audience hall and read Empress Dowager Chongde’s decree: “The dynasty is in peril; Emperors Mu and Ai died young; no successor has been born and the eastern palace is vacant.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王奕親則母弟，故以入纂大位。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye Yi in kinship is the younger brother by the same mother; therefore he was caused to enter and continue the great position.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Langye was the late emperor’s full brother, which is why he was raised to the throne.

sentences.zh: 不圖德之不建，乃至于斯。

translations.literal: We did not expect that virtue would not be established, and it has come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought his rule would prove so devoid of virtue?

sentences.zh: 昏濁潰亂，動違禮度。

translations.literal: Dark, turbid, collapsed, and chaotic; his motions violate ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: He has sunk into vice and confusion and every act breaches ritual.

sentences.zh: 有此三孽，莫知誰子。

translations.literal: There are these three offspring; none knows whose sons they are.
translations.idiomatic: Three bastards have appeared, and no one knows their true father.

sentences.zh: 人倫道喪，醜聲遐布。

translations.literal: Human relations are lost; ugly rumor spreads far.
translations.idiomatic: Decency is shattered and scandal spreads throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 旣不可以奉守社稷，敬承宗廟，且昏孽並大，便欲建樹儲籓。

translations.literal: He already cannot be employed to uphold the altars of soil and grain or reverently inherit the ancestral temples; moreover the dark offspring are all grown, and he intends to establish them as heirs of the princely screen.
translations.idiomatic: He can no longer safeguard the altars or honor the shrines of his ancestors, and those illegitimate children are nearly grown—he means to make them crown princes.

sentences.zh: 誣罔祖宗，頌移皇基，是而可忍，孰不可懷！

translations.literal: He deceives and insults the ancestors, wishing to shift the imperial foundation; if this may be endured, what may not be cherished!
translations.idiomatic: He would hoodwink the spirits of his forebears and steal the mandate itself—if that is tolerable, nothing is intolerable!

sentences.zh: 今廢奕爲東海王，以王還第，供衛之儀，皆如漢朝昌邑故事。

translations.literal: Now depose Yi as Prince of Donghai; let the prince return to his residence; the observances of provision and guard shall all follow the precedent of the Han dynasty’s Marquis of Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi is therefore degraded to prince of Donghai and sent home under guard, exactly as Liu He the marquis of Changyi was treated under the Han.

sentences.zh: 但未亡人不幸，罹此百憂，感念存沒，心焉如割。

translations.literal: But we, the not-yet-deceased, are unlucky and have fallen into these hundred sorrows; moved, we think of the living and the dead; our heart is as though cut.
translations.idiomatic: I am left alone with ill fortune and grief beyond counting; thinking of what has been lost tears me apart.

sentences.zh: 社稷大計，義不獲已。

translations.literal: The great plan for altars of soil and grain, in righteousness, cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The fate of the dynasty leaves no honourable alternative.

sentences.zh: 臨紙悲塞，如何可言。

translations.literal: Facing the paper, grief chokes us; how can words speak it.
translations.idiomatic: Grief chokes this brush—what language could suffice?

sentences.zh: 」于是百官入太極前殿，卽日桓溫使散騎侍郎劉享收帝璽綬。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the hundred officials entered the front hall of Supreme Ultimate; that same day Huan Wen sent Cavalier Gentleman for Employment Liu Xiang to seize the imperial seals and cords.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officials filed into the Taiqiandian, and that same day Huan Wen had Liu Xiang, cavalier gentleman for employment, confiscate the imperial seal and ribbon.

sentences.zh: 帝著白帢單衣，步下西堂，乘犢車出神獸門。

translations.literal: The emperor wore a white kerchief and single garment, stepped down from the West Hall, and rode a calf cart out the Divine Beast Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged in plain white cap and robe, walked down from the West Hall, and left by calf-cart through the Divine Beast Gate.

sentences.zh: 羣臣拜辭，莫不覷欷。

translations.literal: The host of ministers bowed in farewell; none did not sniffle with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers bowed their farewells, many weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 侍御史、殿中監將兵百人衛送東海第。

translations.literal: Palace secretary and palace inspector led a hundred troops to guard and escort him to the Donghai residence.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial secretary and palace inspector marched him under escort of a hundred guards to the Donghai mansion.

sentences.zh: 初，桓溫有不臣之心，欲先立功河朔，以收時望。

translations.literal: Originally, Huan Wen harbored a heart of disloyalty to his lord; he wished first to establish merit north of the He, thereby to harvest the acclaim of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had long nursed treasonous ambition and meant first to win glory on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 及枋頭之敗，威名頓挫，逐潛謀廢立，以長威權。

translations.literal: When the defeat at Fangtou came, his martial reputation suddenly suffered setback; he then secretly plotted deposition and enthronement, thereby to extend his coercive authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fangtou ruined his prestige, so he turned to ousting the emperor as a way to rebuild his terror.

sentences.zh: 然憚帝守道，恐招時議。

translations.literal: Yet he feared the emperor’s guarding of the Way, and dreaded provoking discussion of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he hesitated, knowing the sovereign bore himself correctly and fearing public outcry.

sentences.zh: 以宮闡重悶，床笫易誣，乃言帝爲閹，遂行廢辱。

translations.literal: Because the inner palace was heavy and closed, and the bed-curtains easy to slander, he then declared the emperor a eunuch, thereupon proceeding with deposition and humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The harem’s secrecy made libel easy: he fabricating that the emperor was a castrate and on that pretext carried out the deposition.

sentences.zh: 初，帝平生每以爲慮，嘗召術人扈謙筮之，卦成，答曰：「晉室有磐石之固，陛下有出宮之象。

translations.literal: Originally, through his life the emperor often took this as a worry; he once summoned the technician Hu Qian to milfoil-divine it; when the hexagram was completed, he answered: “The house of Jin has the solidity of a great stone; Your Majesty has an image of leaving the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long been uneasy and once asked the diviner Hu Qian to cast the milfoil; when the lines formed, Hu said: “Jin’s house stands firm as bedrock, yet Your Majesty’s lot shows departure from the palace.

sentences.zh: 」竟如其言。

translations.literal: ” In the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: ” Events unfolded exactly as he foretold.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孝宗因繦抱之姿，用母氏之化，中外無事，十有餘年。

translations.literal: The historians say: Emperor Xiaozong, relying on the posture of swaddling-clothes, employed his mother’s transforming influence; inside and outside there were no incidents for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The chroniclers observe that Emperor Mu, a child on the throne under maternal regency, presided over a decade of outward calm.

sentences.zh: 以武安之才，啓之疆埸；

translations.literal: With Wu’an-caliber talent, he opened the borderlands;
translations.idiomatic: A commander of Wu’an-like prowess pushed the frontiers;

sentences.zh: 以文王之風，被乎江漢，則孔子所謂吾無間然矣。

translations.literal: with the air of a kingly Wen, it spread over the Jiang and the Han—then what Confucius called “I find no fault in him.”
translations.idiomatic: and a kingly civility spread across the middle Yangzi—precisely the perfection Confucius said admitted no reproach.

sentences.zh: 哀皇寬惠，可以爲君，而鴻祀禳天，用塵其德。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai was magnanimous and could have been a lord, yet great sacrifices to pray to Heaven smeared his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai was gentle enough to rule well, but lavish heavenly cults and elixir folly tarnished his name.

sentences.zh: 東海違許龍之駕，屈放命之臣，所謂柔弱勝剛強，得盡于天年者也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai refused Xu Long’s carriage, yielded to ministers who defied command—what is called the soft overcoming the hard, obtaining fulfillment of Heaven-allotted years.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Donghai rebuffed Xu Long’s forged summons and bent before ministers who had defied heaven’s mandate—weakness outlasting force—so he lived out his natural years.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：委裘稱化，大孝爲宗，遵彼聖善，成茲允恭。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Letting the robe rest, they called it transformation; supreme filial piety made the ancestor; following that sacred goodness, this yielding reverence was perfected.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict runs: regency seemed effortless filial rule; sagely virtue shaped humble obedience.

sentences.zh: 西旌玉壘，北旆金墉。

translations.literal: West they flew banners toward Jade Rampart; north they planted pennons at Golden Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Banners waved toward Shu’s jade cliffs and Luoyang’s golden bastions.

sentences.zh: 遷殷舊僰，莫不來從。

translations.literal: They moved Yin’s old Bo tribes; none failed to come and follow.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples once beyond the pale were drawn into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 哀后寬仁，惟靈旣集。

translations.literal: Emperor Ai was generous and humane; only baleful portents had already gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai ruled gently, yet heaven answered only with gathering ill omens.

sentences.zh: 海西多故，時災見及。

translations.literal: Haixi knew many vicissitudes; seasonal calamities appeared and reached him.
translations.idiomatic: The Haixi duke’s age was tempestuous; disaster pressed upon him from every side.

sentences.zh: 彼異阿衡，我非昌邑。

translations.literal: Their case differs from Yi Yin the regulator; we were not Changyi.
translations.idiomatic: That coup was no Yi Yin restoring order; our emperor was no Liu He of Changyi.
